fills.reason: Searched all src/main Kotlin/Java for SecretKeySpec, IvParameterSpec, javax.crypto, KeyGenerator, Cipher.getInstance: no app-level cryptography exists, so no keys are hardcoded in code.

Logging goes through Timber (DebugTree only for debug builds, a crash-reporting tree in production). Searched Timber calls for password, hkey, token, username, email: the only hits log that a value is missing, never the value itself.

Info.kt enables JavaScript and allowContentAccess, and other WebViews leave content access at its default, but setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is never set to true anywhere, so the fail condition (all three) is not met.

The card viewers set javaScriptEnabled and allowFileAccess to true, but neither allowFileAccessFromFileURLs nor allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is set anywhere (both default false above API 16), so the third fail condition is not met.
The only credential form is the AnkiWeb login: the password field uses textPassword and the username field textNoSuggestions|textEmailAddress, both non-caching input types.

No FLAG_SECURE, setRecentsScreenshotEnabled or similar API is used anywhere in src/main. The login screen masks the password; whether flashcard content or the account screen is sensitive enough to need screenshot protection is the owner's call.
Notifications show review-reminder titles, cards-due counts and sync progress/errors; none carry credentials, OTPs or other sensitive data.
The AnkiWeb password field is a TextInputEditField with inputType textPassword (masked, with a user-controlled visibility toggle); no Compose TextField is used for credentials.

JS bridges exist (AnkiDroidKeyboard.setNoSuggest in the card WebView, bridgeCommandInterface on local pages, ankidroid/ankidroidSave in DeckOptions), but the one reachable from untrusted card HTML only toggles keyboard suggestions, and the others are on pages served from the app's local server with navigation restricted.

The app has a login screen (AnkiWeb credentials) and no overlay protection anywhere: no filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED checks or setHideOverlayWindows in src/main.

evidence.detail: Password field on the login screen has no filterTouchesWhenObscured or other tapjacking protection.
